 Heard.
02.

The petitioner is seeking a declaration that the land belonging to him, bearing Gat No.20,
situated at village Mhaispur-Mocharda, District Amravati, admeasuring 0.62 hectare, which was acquired under the award dated 13/04/1999 passed by respondent No. 2, stands released from acquisition in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner moved an application seeking permission to raise an additional ground saying that the award itself is not legally tenable, as the same was not passed within the stipulated period prescribed under the law.

03. The argument of the learned Counsel for the petitioner is that, in view of the stand taken by respondent No. 2, the present petition could be disposed of by directing the respondent to publish a notice in terms of sub- section (1) of Section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Our attention is invited to paragraphs 3 and 4 of the reply filed by respondent No.2, which read thus:

1 "3.
Moreover, vide letter dated 24.02.2026, the Village Revenue Officer has intimated to respondent No.2 that there is no need to expand the village extension.

The copy of letter issued by Village Revenue Officer to the respondent No.2 is annexed herewith as Annexure R-2.
4.
It is humbly submitted that spot inspection of the land which belongs to the petitioner was done by Village Revenue Officer on 02.03.2026.
The report issued by the said officer shows that the petitioner is in possession of the said disputed land and is cultivating the same.

The copy of report dated 02.03.2026 issued by Village Revenue Officer is annexed herewith as Annexure R-3."
04.
As could be seen, the Village Revenue Officer, vide communication dated 24/02/2026, had informed respondent No.2 that there is no necessity to expand the Gaothan area of the village.
It further appears that the petitioner is in possession of the disputed land.
Accordingly, respondent No. 2 has requested to pass an appropriate order in the matter.

05. In our view, if the respondents intend to withdraw from the acquisition of any land of which possession has been not taken, the appropriate recourse is to publish a notification in terms of sub-section (1) of Section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shanti Sports Club and another vs. Union of India and others - (2009) 15 SCC 705.
06.

sentences.text: The respondents shall go through the said judgment and take an appropriate decision within a period of two weeks from today.

07. List the matter on 22nd April, 2026.
